title: Box a decorated cake for a customer without touching the frosting
instruction: Box the decorated cake for the customer: slide it into the cake box on its board, close the box and tuck the lid's tab in, without touching the frosting.
context: Boxing a decorated cake is a familiar moment for most people: a birthday or celebration cake is handed over at a bakery or supermarket counter in a window cake box, and leftover cake is boxed again to carry home. Anyone who has done it knows the risk: the board has to slide in level and the lid has to close without smudging the piped frosting. The 10 x 10 x 5 in lock-corner window box is used exactly as it comes: its front panel, unlocked, springs back up off the counter, so one hand holds it flat while the other slides the cake in straight by its 247.6 mm board rim, between the two corner gussets that stand up at the front corners (3.2 mm clearance per side); then the front panel is lifted and squared, the window lid brought down and its front tab tucked inside the front panel. Closest accepted look-alike: TK-8A2A64 (crimp a foil pan rim onto a flat board lid); here a fragile piped cake is slid through a sprung carton front and the box is closed by tucking a paperboard tab.
setup: Two 6-DOF arms with parallel-jaw grippers sit at (0.00, +0.305) m and (0.00, -0.305) m along a smooth wipeable bakery counter (top z = 0.7475 m). Three loose 1:1 objects start on the counter: (1) a white 24-pt (0.6 mm) SBS paperboard 10 x 10 x 5 in lock-corner window bakery box (BRP Box Shop #245, USD 29.36/10-pack or USD 117.42/100-pack at brpboxshop.com/245.html; Southern Champion Tray #23053 family; 254.0 x 254.0 x 127.0 mm inner cavity, ~0.146 kg estimated, counter friction 0.52), used as it comes with no cuts, tape or added parts: back and side walls erected with the two rear lock tabs hooked, the two front lock tabs left unhooked so the 251.0 x 126.0 mm front panel folds down on its bottom crease. Its centre is at (0.429, +0.143) m, turned +68 deg so its open front faces the right arm. The front panel rests 15 deg above the counter (the unlocked crease springs back). Each front corner keeps the box's own gusset, a 123 mm square web folded on its diagonal that joins the front panel to the side wall: with the panel flat it stands upright in line with the side wall; as the panel rises it folds into the panel's inside corner. The hinged 257.2 x 257.2 mm lid (174 x 174 mm clear window) starts open at 95 deg along the back wall with its tapered 35.0 mm front tuck tab at 45 deg outward. (2) A fabricated 247.6 mm OD x 4.8 mm thick (~0.055 kg, sliding friction 0.20) silver-foil-topped corrugated cake circle centred on the box's axis 400 mm in front of the box's centre, at (0.279, -0.228) m (its edge 23 mm short of the lowered front panel's edge), made per shipped 1:1 template tasks/cake-box/fab/cake_board_template.svg by laminating two 10 in nominal Wilton corrugated white cake circles (MFR 191001569, USD 11.49/12-pack at WebstaurantStore #143191001569, ~254 mm stock OD, ~2.4 mm/ply) at 90 deg crossed flutes with PVA glue, wrapping the top face with 0.018 mm household aluminium foil, trimming to 247.6 +/- 0.5 mm OD with a 3.0 x 1.2 mm bottom kraft bevel, and checking OD, 4.8 +/- 0.4 mm thickness and 55 +/- 6 g mass before use. (3) A reusable cold decorated cake stand-in fixed centred on the board with a royal-icing dab: an 8 x 3 in (203.2 x 76.2 mm) round polystyrene foam cake dummy (NY Cake, USD 7.99) covered in 2.4 mm pastel blush rolled fondant (208.0 mm body OD, 78.6 mm height) with hardened white royal-icing bottom and top piped shell borders (108.5 mm max radius, leaving a 15.3 mm exposed silver board rim) and eight top swirl rosettes (93.5 mm peak height; 0.300 kg estimated, cake-to-board effective friction ~1.70). As at a bakery counter, the cake is moved by pushing the exposed board rim across the counter and the lowered front panel, not lifted.
scoring: Whole-trial sticky zero if at any step: any robot collision hull, box panel or corner gusset comes within 1.0 mm of the cake's frosting (side fondant, bottom/top piped borders, top face, and rosettes, sampled <= 3.2 mm apart; bottom resting on board excluded); the cake tilts over 10.0 deg, slides over 10.0 mm, or lifts over 3.0 mm on its board; the board leaves the counter or box base by over 20.0 mm; or any box panel is forced past its crease stop (crushed). Otherwise, final state after 21 consecutive samples (1.0 s at 20 Hz) during which all six fingertip/pad points remain at least 80.0 mm from every box panel and gusset, the board, and the cake and all tracked 3D object points move under 1.0 mm all-pairs: 0.25 if the 247.6 mm cylindrical board's analytic 3D projection lies within the 254.0 x 254.0 mm inner base plus a 1.0 mm wall-contact/ruler allowance per side (projected half-extents <= 128.0 mm in X and Y, bottom face within 3.5 mm of the base floor); 0.5 if 0.25 holds and the front panel is within 5.0 deg of vertical; 0.75 if 0.5 holds and the window lid is within 5.0 deg of flat and within 3.0 mm of the 127.0 mm walls' tops all round; 1.0 if 0.75 holds and the lid's front tab is tucked inside the front panel with its free edge at least 10.0 mm behind the front panel's inner face (and at least 8.0 mm below its top edge); untouched start scores 0. Real trial: off-table over a tray, brush a thin film of food-grade unsweetened cocoa powder onto removable wipeable gripper-pad sleeves and the lid/tab underside before each trial (any brown mark on the white borders, rosettes, or pastel fondant, or any dent under a low-angle raking lamp, scores 0), record synchronised 30 fps overhead and side video (contact, drops, 1.0 s released stillness), check <= 1.0 mm board overhang past the 254 x 254 mm inner base lines, <= 3.0 mm lid-to-wall gap all round, >= 10.0 mm tab tuck depth, and >= 80.0 mm six-point hand clearance with a 1 mm steel ruler and 80 mm gauge block, then run the prospective retention check by lifting the closed carton 50 mm by its side walls and tilting 30 +/- 2 deg forward against a 30 deg wedge for 3 s to verify the front panel and tab stay tucked. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
fidelity: 0.6 mm SBS board uses 0.8-1.6 mm rigid panels with estimated crease friction (0.008-0.085 N*m) and a 0.4 N*m/rad front crease spring-back below 15 deg up. Each gusset is two 0.5 mm triangles on 0.08 N*m/rad sprung hinges set by the front panel's angle; they meet hands, board and cake. Tab: hinged flap, 0.001 N*m/rad spring, 14.5 mm root relief. Icing/fondant are rigid meshes with a 1 mm contact latch; masses estimated; demo reads poses.
reset_notes: Cold room-temperature stand-in props only, on a wipeable food-safe counter mat; wear clean nitrile gloves (and safety glasses when cutting the board template). Before use, check the fabricated foil board (fab/cake_board_template.svg) with calipers (4.8 +/- 0.4 mm), a 1 mm steel ruler (247.6 +/- 0.5 mm OD) and a 1 g scale (55 +/- 6 g). Use a box as it comes: rear lock tabs hooked, front lock tabs unhooked, no tape; replace the box if a crease is crushed or the front panel no longer springs back to 15 +/- 5 deg above the counter (protractor). Off-table over a catch tray, never near robot joints, lightly brush food-grade unsweetened cocoa powder onto removable nitrile/silicone fingertip sleeves and the lid/tab underside. Place the box centred at (0.429, 0.143) m turned +68 deg with the front panel resting on its own (15 deg up), lid open (~95 deg) and tab outward (~45 deg), and set the cake on its board at (0.279, -0.228) m, handling only the 15.3 mm rim. Between trials wipe the mat and sleeves with a damp cloth and brush off or re-cover marked icing.
